name: Information Processing & Management: SI 'Multilingual and Multimodal Solutions for Low Resource, Indigenous, Endangered Languages and Dialects'
apc: Hybrid (subscription option, no fee; OA APC applies if chosen)
notes: Best topical fit: the CFP explicitly lists 'applications of LLMs and VLMs to low-resource settings', corpus/dataset construction and multimodal (text+image) approaches. A Vietnamese detailed-caption dataset plus verified-proposition supervision fits it directly. Review is rolling ('reviewed on a rolling basis... early submission strongly encouraged'), with double-blind review via submit.elsevier.com/IPM. Risk: this is a high-bar Q1 venue, and Vietnamese is low-resource but not endangered or indigenous, so frame it as low-resource multimodal. Extension of the FAIR 2026 paper is allowed only as substantially new work (aim for 30%+ new content); disclose the conference version and cite it. The CFP itself does not state an extension policy.

name: Pattern Recognition: SI 'Multimodal Representation Learning Based on Vision Foundation Models'
notes: Its topics include instruction tuning for aligning vision with language, PEFT, evaluation and benchmarks for robustness and fairness, and video-language applications. VSPS fits under training paradigms plus evaluation. Risk: the issue is representation-learning oriented, so the method must be framed as alignment/fine-tuning of a VFM-based VLM. Pattern Recognition is very selective. Extension of the FAIR 2026 paper is allowed only as substantially new work (aim for 30%+ new content); disclose the conference version and cite it. The CFP itself does not state an extension policy.

name: International Journal of Computer Vision: SI 'Multimodal Large Language Models for Unified Comprehension and Generation'
review_time: Median 37 days to first decision (journal page)
notes: Topics include instruction tuning and preference alignment for multimodal systems, grounded multimodal reasoning, and an evaluation track covering robustness, calibration, reliability and safety. Hallucination-reducing supervision fits under alignment plus reliability. The CFP explicitly allows expanded versions of previous work if reuse is disclosed. Risk: only 3 weeks remain, IJCV is a top venue, and the 'unified comprehension+generation' framing is broader than captioning.

name: Complex & Intelligent Systems: Collection 'Multimodal Perception and Foundation Models for Intelligent Systems'
apc: Open access, APC applies (amount not verified)
review_time: Median 20 days to first decision (journal page)
notes: Topics explicitly list vision-language models, LLMs in perception systems, multimodal learning and representation learning. The scope is broad, so a VLM hallucination-reduction paper fits squarely. Fully open access, so expect an APC (amount not shown on the collection page; check the journal's fees page). Q1 in SJR but generally less selective than PR/IJCV, which makes it a realistic target. Extension of the FAIR 2026 paper is allowed only as substantially new work (aim for 30%+ new content); disclose the conference version and cite it. The CFP itself does not state an extension policy.

name: Applied Soft Computing: SI 'Novel Multimodal Foundation Models in Applied Computing and Intelligence' (VSI:ASOC_MFM)
notes: Topics include VLMs and their extensions, and multimodal training and optimisation. Select 'VSI:ASOC_MFM' as the article type. Risk: the CFP states 'each submission must contribute to soft computing related methodology', so VSPS would need a soft-computing angle (e.g. fuzzy or uncertainty-based verifier scoring) or it risks desk rejection. Extension of the FAIR 2026 paper is allowed only as substantially new work (aim for 30%+ new content); disclose the conference version and cite it. The CFP itself does not state an extension policy.

name: Information Processing & Management: SI 'Trustworthy Content Governance and Safe Generative AI in the Age of Large Language Models'
notes: The CFP lists 'Safety evaluation: hallucination detection, bias mitigation, toxicity reduction' and names hallucinations as a core risk. VSPS fits as hallucination mitigation in generative VLMs. Risk: the issue is oriented to governance and safety of LLM content rather than vision, so stress the verification and trustworthiness framing. Extension of the FAIR 2026 paper is allowed only as substantially new work (aim for 30%+ new content); disclose the conference version and cite it. The CFP itself does not state an extension policy.
